highlights:
Cape Verde arrive ranked 69th in the world, eight places below Saudi Arabia at 61st. Neither side enters this fixture in strong form. The Blue Sharks have drawn three of their last five matches, while Saudi Arabia have lost their last three. Form tables tell one story, but knockout football rewrites the script.

Tactically, this is a game between two flawed sides. Saudi Arabia have more experience and better individual quality at the top end, but their defensive problems are real and documented. Cape Verde are organised, disciplined, and have the pace to hurt a high defensive line. The Blue Sharks may be debutants, but they qualified with a 100% home record in African qualifying. They know how to win under pressure.
[...]
The X-factor in this match is the occasion itself. Cape Verde will be playing their first-ever World Cup game just eleven days before this fixture, against Spain. By the time they face Saudi Arabia on June 26, they will have experienced the World Cup atmosphere. That could free them up rather than tighten them. Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, arrive knowing they have just been humiliated at home by Egypt. A squad with shaken confidence against a team with nothing to lose is a dangerous combination. According to CAF Online, Cape Verde called up five new players in their final pre-tournament tune-up, which signals Bubista is still shaping his final competitive setup.
[...]
Saudi Arabia still have enough class to edge this, particularly if Al-Dawsari is at his best. But Cape Verde will make it extremely difficult, and the group stage format gives third-placed teams a real chance to progress. A draw would not be a surprise, but Saudi Arabia’s need for three points may force them to overcommit and leave space for Cape Verde to exploit.
[...]
Our Prediction: Saudi Arabia 1-1 Cape Verde
[...]
Al-Dawsari gets Saudi Arabia in front with a moment of individual brilliance, but Cape Verde equalise from a set piece in the second half. Both sides finish the match knowing they still have work to do in their final group game.

highlights:
Saudi Arabia arrive at the 2026 World Cup still living off the greatest group-stage upset in history — beating Lionel Messi's Argentina 2-1 in Qatar 2022. Georgios Donis has since built a more organized tactical unit. Salem Al-Dawsari remains the attacking threat — direct, fast, and capable of a world-class moment. Saud Abdulhamid (Roma) is the best Saudi player in European football. The squad
[...]
heavily influenced by Saudi Pro League investment — quality has improved but the gap to the world's best remains large. Group H with Spain and Uruguay — Saudi Arabia realistically fights Cape Verde for third or fourth. Totals: UNDER — Mancini defends deep and counter-attacks
[...]
Saudi Arabia under Georgios Donis play a 4-5-1 defensive block that absorbs pressure and lives for Al-Dawsari moments on the counter. The Argentina win proved this system can execute to perfection on the right day. In Group H, they face Spain (the tournament favorite) and Uruguay (Bielsa's elite pressing side). The realistic ceiling is a point from Cape Verde and a competitive showing vs Spain or Uruguay
